name: Labradford
label: Kranky
lede: Labradford took its name from a Louisville basketball player, and its first 7-inch landed on the desk of a Chicago distributor so squarely that two men there started Kranky just to release the album. Years later the band drifted to a stop without ever announcing one.

eras.title: A label built for one record
eras.text: Labradford began in Richmond, Virginia as a duo: Mark Nelson on guitar, tapes and voice, Carter Brown on analog synths and organ. Their slow, dark drone rock sounded like nothing around them, and it reached exactly the right desk in Chicago.

years.src: Chicago Reader: Labradford (2001) · Weedbus 13: Labradford · Brainwashed: Labradford
years.h: Mark Nelson and Carter Brown start a band in Richmond
years.p: Nelson plays guitar; Brown, who had studied organ in Richmond for two years, plays old analog synths. Treated guitar and keyboards are the sound from the start.

years.h: A Louisville basketball player lends the band its name
years.p: Bassist Robert Donne told the Weedbus fanzine the name comes from LaBradford Smith, who played for Louisville and went on to the NBA's Washington Bullets.

years.h: A 7-inch called Everlast goes out on Retro 8
years.p: The small Retro 8 label also puts a Labradford track on its compilation Repugnating the Wombat.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily: Kranky Celebrates 25 Years · Chicago Reader: Kranky and Proud of It · Wikipedia: Kranky
years.h: Two Cargo employees start a label to release one band
years.p: Joel Leoschke, Cargo's domestic buyer, gets the Labradford 7-inch and says of the band: "What they were doing was so uncommercial, so unique, and so compelling." With colleague Bruce Adams, a former Touch and Go publicist, he founds Kranky.
years.xp:
Leoschke had spent five years as Cargo's domestic buyer and knew how new labels failed. They nearly called it Curmudgeon, but Leoschke said it had too many syllables.

Three decades on, the roster runs from [[Godspeed You! Black Emperor|3648db01-b29d-4ab9-835c-83f6a5068fe4]] to [[Deerhunter|4f416ed7-dda2-45de-a6f1-b986e861cf4b]], and Labradford is still krank 001.

years.src: Wikipedia: Prazision LP · John Peel Wiki: Labradford
years.h: Prazision LP becomes krank 001
years.p: Recorded at McKinley Hall and the Belt Trade Center in Richmond, with Brown on Memorymoog, Polymoog and a Roland vocoder. [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] had played the debut single that year and kept the album in his collection.

eras.title: The vocals leave, the strings arrive
eras.text: With bassist Robert Donne, an old Richmond friend from the hard rock band Breadwinner, Labradford started writing as a trio and let the vocals slip away. Strings, chains and live percussion crept in, and Stars of the Lid and Stereolab became company.

q: they just asked me to join and have a go at playing with them
yt: Live at Lounge Ax, Chicago, February 12, 1994
years.h: Robert Donne, an old friend from Breadwinner, joins the duo
years.p: Donne had known Brown for about ten years. After Prazision LP, Brown and Mark Nelson simply asked him in.
years.xp: Donne played in the hard rock band Breadwinner before Labradford. He told Weedbus that from the time he joined, "we started again," the three of them writing songs together instead of leaning on the duo's older material.

years.src: John Peel Wiki: Labradford · Wikipedia: Labradford
years.h: Labradford records for John Peel, and Radio 1 airs it a month later
years.p: Four tracks air on [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]]'s BBC Radio 1 show on November 19: Starcity, Accelerating on a Smoother Road, Balanced on Its Own Flame and Comfort.
years.xp: The session was recorded on October 16. The band also lands on Virgin's Ambient 4: Isolationism compilation around this time.

years.h: A Stable Reference arrives with Donne and without vocals
years.p: Recorded at American University in Washington, D.C. AllMusic's Ned Raggett notes that lyrics disappear from nearly every track.

years.src: Getintothis: Labradford buyer's guide · Wikipedia: Labradford
years.h: Stereolab and Tortoise take Labradford on tour
years.p: Labradford supports [[Stereolab|f1df0431-9250-4ec8-95d8-f19ce7cf7fb6]] and [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]] in 1995, after earlier dates opening for [[Archers of Loaf|7cf05db3-24e7-4534-84bf-65006cd0cc82]]. Merge Records also releases the Julius 7-inch.

years.src: Weedbus 13: Labradford · John Peel Wiki: Labradford · Wikipedia: Labradford
years.h: Robert Donne says the chains on Labradford are played live
years.p: The self-titled third album adds string arrangements by classical violinist Chris Johnston. Donne says the chains scraping on Phantom Channel Crossing are not samples.
years.xp:
"They're all played live!" Donne told Weedbus of the rattling and scraping sounds. Johnston, a friend, helped write the string quartet arrangements.

A second Peel session followed in May 1996. That year Labradford also split the Kahanek Incident, Vol. 3 12-inch with Austin's [[Stars of the Lid|a1154343-1ea1-4007-97d3-2382482a90cd]] on Trance Syndicate, and put out Scenic Recovery on Stereolab's Duophonic label.

years.h: A string section and Fender Rhodes arrive on Mi Media Naranja
years.p: Labradford's fourth Kranky album has a Spanish idiom for one's other half as its title. Brainwashed notes the strings, Rhodes and slide guitar now filling out the sound.

eras.title: Curators, then a quiet stop
eras.text: Labradford became curators as much as a band, putting its name on London festivals with Brian Eno's music and Tony Conrad on the bill. By the end the three lived in different cities, made one last record with Steve Albini, and quietly stopped.

years.src: Cerysmatic Factory: The LaBradford First Annual Festival of Drifting
years.h: Labradford takes over London's South Bank for ten days
years.p: The first Festival of Drifting fills the Royal Festival Hall, Queen Elizabeth Hall and Purcell Room, with Brian Eno's Music for Airports, John Martyn, Tony Conrad, Pan Sonic and [[Michael Gira|8d936df1-9da6-4b11-87c3-7bb8fd8a62c4]].
years.xp: Presented by Foundation, the BBC and Blast First, Labradford's UK label, the festival ran to October 3. The bill also had The Durutti Column, Charlemagne Palestine, Bill Nelson and writer Iain Sinclair.

years.h: Nelson's side project Pan American debuts on Kranky
years.p: Pan American, started in 1997 for music too electronic for Labradford, becomes one of Kranky's longest-running names.

years.src: Cerysmatic Factory: Labradford 2nd Festival of Drifting 1999 · Wikipedia: Labradford · Brainwashed: Labradford
years.h: The second Festival of Drifting moves into a working church
years.p: Four nights at Union Chapel in Islington, with spin-off shows in Sheffield and Edinburgh. Wikipedia lists [[Sigur Rós|f6f2326f-6b25-4170-b89d-e235b25508e8]], [[Matmos|46e8a8ee-d2cd-4165-9725-02f72d0027a9]], Pole and [[Papa M|6edbe0fb-734e-4b1d-9c64-73ebb04853e1]] among the series' acts.

years.h: E Luxo So names its six tracks after the people on them
years.p: Recorded at Sound of Music in Richmond, with strings and dulcimer by Peter Neff. Every title is a list of the players and engineers.
years.xp: NME gave it 8 out of 10; Pitchfork gave it 5.3. Released by Blast First in the UK and Kranky in the US.

yt: Live at Lounge Ax, Chicago, September 16, 1999
years.h: Godspeed You! Black Emperor and Labradford cross North America
years.p: By now the three live in Richmond, Washington, D.C. and Chicago, and they cross North America with [[Godspeed You! Black Emperor|3648db01-b29d-4ab9-835c-83f6a5068fe4]].

years.big: "Distills its once amorphous and sprawling music to its essence"
years.h: Labradford plans to play Fixed::Context straight through at Schubas
years.p: The Chicago Reader's verdict on the new album, ahead of a Schubas show where all four pieces are played in order. Brown has swapped synths for piano and organ, and Nelson has stopped singing.

years.h: Four pieces with Steve Albini turn out to be the last
years.p: Fixed::Context was recorded in July 2000 at Electrical Audio in Chicago with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], for Blast First and Kranky. The Guardian heard Duane Eddy playing the Twin Peaks theme.
years.xp: No breakup was ever announced, and Labradford has released nothing since. Wikipedia notes that Coil were friends who had planned to collaborate with the band.

eras.title: Never broke up, never came back
eras.text: Labradford has never officially disbanded. Two-thirds of the band reunited under a new name, and its music turned up somewhere nobody expected: a prestige TV drama about a fictional pope.

years.src: Fact: Kranky reveals · Getintothis: Labradford buyer's guide · Brainwashed: Labradford
years.h: Nelson and Donne return as Anjou, with Steven Hess on drums
years.p: The two Labradford members and Pan American drummer [[Steven Hess|f6e3c48b-fe51-42b0-b002-9d77da680442]] release Anjou on Kranky after four years' work. A second album, Epithymía, follows in 2017.
years.xp: In the Labradford silence Donne had made Aix Em Klemm with [[Stars of the Lid|a1154343-1ea1-4007-97d3-2382482a90cd]]'s [[Adam Wiltzie|fa7d8199-ba6a-448c-b25a-a615261fe6e6]], recorded as Cristal, played with Spokane and toured with [[Gregor Samsa|3c651564-eb88-48e0-a862-d6db17e8464a]]. He also played bass on Pan American's 2013 album.

years.h: The Young Pope puts Labradford on HBO
years.p: The E Luxo So track titled for its credits, Chris Johnston, Craig Markva, Jamie Evans, plays across several episodes of Paolo Sorrentino's series, fifteen years after the band's last release.
